_doc: THE ONE declaration of the Cloud SuperApp's users (#573): User (1) -> identities (N, exactly ONE primary) -> peers (N, exactly ONE primary) -> auth_providers. The derive engine emits ONE build-cloud-superapp-<slug>.json per key here (served bearer-gated at /pub/superapp/config/<slug>), so adding a user, an identity or a peer is a DATA addition — no code change. `profile` maps 1:1 onto the app's ProfilePrefs keys. Nothing in the app's Kotlin names a user, an address or a device: it reads this file's emitted form.
_doc_identities: The addresses that are this user. `primary` marks the one the profile, the mail 2FA code and the Authelia bearer belong to; the others are the same person's other mailboxes on the same domain. Exactly one primary, or the deriver refuses.
_doc_peers: The user's devices, keyed by the id the vault's staged peers section uses (cloud-vault configs/peers/sources.json). `wg_client` is the row on BOTH meshes (cloud-infra config.json#native.wireguard.clients and cloud-u-containers/infra-net_wireguard-public/build.json#wireguard_public.clients) — the peer's mesh identity is READ from there, never restated here. `vault_wg_dir` is the vault directory (A0_keys/providers/wireguard/<dir>) whose config-* files are this peer's wg-quick profiles; regen-superapp-wireguard-profiles.js reads every peer that declares one, redacts the PrivateKey and emits superapp-wireguard-profiles.json per peer. `vault_device` is the key the vault's electronics/apps sections use for this device. `primary` marks the ONE peer whose profiles also appear at the artifact's top-level `wireguard` (the block the APK's ui.wireguard_profiles guard mirrors); exactly one, or the deriver refuses.
_doc_auth_providers: Which sign-in providers the superapp may offer this user, in order (the first is primary). The app's build.json::ui.vault_connect.sign_in.providers is the WIRING for each id (endpoints, client ids); this is the POLICY: a provider not listed here is not offered for this user.
_security: NO SECRETS IN THIS FILE. This repo is PUBLIC. WireGuard private keys are never carried by the artifact — see superapp-wireguard-profiles.json.
